li.label: given the last of the medicine
li.description: They spent the last of the medicine on me. I'm trying to get better fast enough to deserve it.

li.label: the medicine is gone
li.description: We used the last of the medicine. Now I keep thinking about who will need it next.

li.label: made do with broth
li.description: The council kept the medicine back and gave me broth and a blanket. I understand why. I'd still rather have had the medicine.

li.label: bitter herb tea
li.description: Someone went out and picked herbs for me and boiled them into a tea. It tasted like a ditch. My chest feels looser.

li.label: found the right herbs
li.description: I knew which leaves to look for and where they'd be growing. They were there.

li.label: kept apart while sick
li.description: They moved my bed away from everyone until I'm better. I know it makes sense. It's lonely in here.

li.label: the sickness kept away
li.description: The sick one sleeps somewhere else now. I can stop listening for coughs in the night.

li.label: they kept me close
li.description: They could have put me in the storeroom while I'm sick. They didn't.

li.label: sleeping next to a cough
li.description: Someone in my room is sick, and the council has left them there. I sleep with my blanket over my face.

li.label: someone sat up with me
li.description: I was sick and someone sat up with me, brought water and changed the cloth on my head. I won't forget it.

li.label: kept out of my kitchen
li.description: I've got a cold, not a broken arm, and they've put someone else at my stove. They'll burn the onions.

li.label: cooked through it
li.description: I kept cooking while I was sick, with a cloth over my face and my hands scrubbed raw. Every meal went out on time.

li.label: food from a sick cook
li.description: The cook is coughing into the stew pot, or near enough. I ate it. I tried not to think about it.

li.label: cold suppers
li.description: The cook is ill, so it's cold food for a few days. Bread, cold meat and whatever's in the jar.

li.label: time to get better
li.description: The council told me to rest until I'm well. I haven't argued.

li.label: an old remedy
li.description: I spent the night wrapped in an old remedy that smelled terrible. This morning I could breathe.

li.label: they let me try my remedy
li.description: The council let me try the cure my family has always used. I'm glad someone still has a use for what I know.

li.label: my remedy refused
li.description: My grandmother's cure has worked for three generations. The council would rather trust a book.

li.label: smelled like a poultice
li.description: I spent a night in a stinking poultice and I'm no better. People step back when I come in.

li.label: the whole house smells of it
li.description: Somebody's cure is stewing by the sickbed and the smell has got into my clothes.

li.label: helped a sick traveler
li.description: A stranger came to us sick, and we gave them a dose from our own shelf. They shook my hand twice.

li.label: gave away our stores
li.description: We gave away things we'll need ourselves before the year is out. Somebody should be keeping count.

li.label: turned away the sick
li.description: Someone sick asked us for help and we said no. I keep thinking about the way they looked at us.

li.label: a strange cure that worked
li.description: A traveler made me do the strangest things to get rid of my illness. I feel better. I'm not going to ask why.

li.label: a cure that didn't
li.description: I let a stranger try a cure on me. I'm just as sick, and now I'm the story at supper.

li.label: slept at last
li.description: The council sent me to bed and put someone else at the sickbed. I slept like a stone, the whole night through.

li.label: others learned to help
li.description: Three more people now know how to change a dressing and take a fever. I'm not the only one awake at night anymore.

li.label: we helped our neighbors
li.description: The people camped near us were in trouble, and we didn't pretend not to see it.

li.label: tended the camp's sick
li.description: I went from bedroll to bedroll at the camp with my bag. Some of them will be on their feet tomorrow because of it.

li.label: showed them where the game is
li.description: I took their hunters out and showed them the trails. They came back with meat, and thanked me as if I'd caught it.

li.label: turned away hungry neighbors
li.description: The people camped near us came asking for food and we sent them back with nothing. I could see their fire from my window.

li.label: found the lost child
li.description: I was the one who found the child, asleep in a hollow with the goat. I carried them back to the camp myself.

li.label: we didn't help them look
li.description: A child was lost out there all night and we stayed in by our own fire. They found the child at dawn. We had nothing to do with it.

li.label: the council heard me out
li.description: I wasn't there when they decided, so they let me have my say afterward. That's fair.

li.label: the same meeting twice
li.description: We sat through it all once already. Now we're sitting through it again because one person wasn't there.

li.label: decided without me, and that's that
li.description: They made up their minds while I was out working, and they won't hear another word about it.

li.label: the meetings will wait for me
li.description: From now on the council waits for those still at work before it starts. Somebody listened.

li.label: supper waits for the meeting
li.description: The council won't start until everyone is in from work, so supper is late and the meetings run into the night.

li.label: they made it up to me
li.description: The council broke its word, then came and made it right. I'll give the next promise more credit.

li.label: an apology at the table
li.description: The council stood up at supper and said they'd let me down. The whole table heard it. That mattered more than I thought it would.

li.label: excuses instead
li.description: I asked why they broke their promise and got a long list of reasons. Reasons aren't what I was promised.

li.label: what the council's word is worth
li.description: The council broke a promise to me and says it owes me nothing for it. I'll remember that the next time they promise anything.

li.label: a few days off
li.description: I asked for a few days off at the worst possible time, and they gave them to me anyway. I slept through most of the first one.

li.label: lighter duties
li.description: I'm on light work for a while: mending, sorting, sitting down for most of it. It isn't a rest, but my back thanks me.

li.label: told to hold on
li.description: I told them I was at the end of my rope. They asked me to hold on until the rush is over.

li.label: a half day each
li.description: We each get a half day off in turn until the worst is over. Mine was this afternoon. I lay in the grass.

li.label: earned my rest
li.description: I've done my share and more. The council agreed. From now on I sit in the sun and mend what I feel like mending.

li.label: passing on what I know
li.description: My hands aren't what they were, but I still know how it's done. Now somebody younger is learning it from me.

li.label: not allowed to stop
li.description: I asked to put down my tools after all these years. The council says they still need me. My back says otherwise.

li.label: a straight answer
li.description: I asked the grown-ups a hard question and they told me the truth. I've been thinking about it all day.

li.label: a story instead
li.description: I asked a question and they told me a story. It wasn't really the answer, but it was a good story.

li.label: a child asked me
li.description: One of the children brought me a question the council couldn't answer, and I could. They listened to all of it.

li.label: told I'm too young
li.description: I asked a real question and they said I'd understand when I'm older. I'll understand now, if somebody tells me.

li.label: real work
li.description: I'm learning a proper trade now, with real tools. My hands are sore. I don't care.

li.label: made it myself
li.description: I made a thing from start to finish, all by myself, and it works. I keep going back to look at it.

li.label: my first try broke
li.description: I made my first thing at the workbench and it came apart in my hands. They said everyone's first one does.

li.label: sent off to play
li.description: I asked to do real work and they told me to go and play. I'm not a baby.

li.label: sent a dead traveler's words home
li.description: We sent the journal back to the traveler's people. Somebody there has been waiting a long time to hear.

li.label: a stranger's journal, read aloud
li.description: We read a dead traveler's journal aloud after supper. The weather they wrote about was our weather.

li.label: someone's private words, read out
li.description: We read a dead stranger's journal out loud for an evening's entertainment. They never wrote it for us.

li.label: laid it to rest
li.description: We buried the traveler's journal under a marker with their name scratched on it.

li.label: something new on the table
li.description: Supper was different for once. I ate it slowly to make it last.

li.label: a kitchen experiment
li.description: The cook tried a new dish tonight. I'd like the old meal back now, please.

li.label: food is food, they said
li.description: I asked for a change at mealtimes and the council told me food is food. Then they went and ate the same thing I did.

li.label: a change of work
li.description: Different tools, a different corner, something else to look at all day. I didn't know how much I needed it.

li.label: learning a new trade
li.description: I'm learning a trade I've never tried, from someone who knows it well. I'm bad at it, and it's the best part of my day.

li.label: chores in rotation
li.description: We all take turns at everything now. I'm no good at half of it, but at least it's different.

li.label: someone has to do it
li.description: I asked for different work. The council said someone has to do mine. Apparently that someone is me, forever.

li.label: a corner of my own
li.description: It's only a corner, with a curtain and a cot, but nobody else sleeps in it.

li.label: supper in two sittings
li.description: We eat in two sittings now. There's room for my elbows, and I can finish a sentence.

li.label: a new room marked out
li.description: There are stakes in the ground and string between them where the new room will go. It's a start.

li.label: everyone is crowded, they said
li.description: I said we're packed in like salted fish. The council said everyone is. That was supposed to help.
